record.title: Marvell announces 2nm 400G-per-lane optical demonstrations aimed at 3.2T AI data-center links
record.summary: In a September 21, 2026 announcement for ECOC, Marvell said it planned to demonstrate 2nm 400G-per-lane optical PAM4 and described it as enabling a transition toward 3.2T data-center connectivity. The company also announced planned 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ pluggables with MACsec and 1.6T ZR/coherent-lite demonstrations. The source establishes the company’s announcement and intended showcase, not independent observation of the demos or measured product performance. It provides no lane power, optical reach, error rate, qualification status or production schedule for the 400G/lane technology.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Marvell announced that it planned to demonstrate a 2nm 400G-per-lane optical PAM4 technology at ECOC 2026 and described it as enabling a transition toward 3.2T data-center connectivity.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The same announcement listed planned 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ pluggable demonstrations with MACsec and 1.6T ZR and coherent-lite O-band demonstrations.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The announcement does not disclose measured power, reach, bit-error rate, interoperability, production qualification or deployment status for the announced 400G-per-lane demonstration.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent observation or measurement of the announced ECOC optical demonstrations was inspected.
The announcement supplies no power per bit, optical reach, bit-error rate, thermal condition or production qualification for the 400G-per-lane optical PAM4 link.

brief.importance_rationale: A working 400G-per-lane optical interface could alter bandwidth density and connectivity choices in large AI fabrics, with downstream effects on rack-scale accelerator designs. This record covers a company-announced planned demonstration; no measured power, reach, error rate, interoperability or production status is established.
limitations: The source is Marvell’s own announcement; the announced technology claims have not been independently measured.
The September 21 release describes demonstrations planned for ECOC, not independent confirmation that the specific demo was successfully completed.
No full link-level performance or production-readiness data are provided.
The projected path to 3.2T describes intended connectivity capability, not a deployed or qualified 3.2T product.

The company also announced planned 2nm 800G ZR/ZR+ pluggables with MACsec and 1.6T ZR/coherent-lite demonstrations. The source establishes the company’s announcement and intended showcase, not independent observation of the demos or measured product performance. technical.claimed_result: Marvell announced plans to demonstrate 2nm 400G/lane optical PAM4 and related 800G and 1.6T optical technologies; its release frames 400G/lane as enabling a transition toward 3.2T data-center connectivity.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected official release verifies that Marvell made these announcement claims and intended to showcase the technologies at ECOC. It does not independently establish the optical performance or successful completion of the planned demos.
technical.mechanism: The announcement concerns optical connectivity components for high-bandwidth data-center links: PAM4 optical signaling at 400G per lane, coherent 800G ZR/ZR+ pluggables with MACsec, and 1.6T ZR and coherent-lite demonstrations. Marvell presents these as steps toward 3.2T connectivity; actual system integration and link-budget evidence were not in the inspected announcement.
technical.regime: Planned showcase at ECOC 2026 in Málaga, September 20–24, 2026. The company announcement is dated September 21, 2026. No measured link length, optical power, error rate, temperature or workload regime is supplied for the 400G/lane technology.
technical.strongest_baseline: Marvell’s own prior disclosed connectivity generations: its release cites 5nm 200G/lane 1.6T Nova DSPs from 2023, a 3nm 1.6T Ara platform in 2024, and 2nm 800G Libra DSPs announced earlier in 2026. This is company-stated roadmap context, not a matched benchmark.

brief.title: Marvell announces 2nm 400G-per-lane optical demonstrations aimed at 3.2T AI data-center links
brief.why_it_matters: If the 400G-per-lane optical link is demonstrated under usable power, reach and error-rate conditions, it could support higher-bandwidth AI data-center fabrics and reduce the number of lanes needed for a 3.2T link. The announcement does not report those conditions or establish deployment readiness, so the consequence remains contingent on measurements and interoperability.
